name: What causes new pool plaster to crack after resurfacing?

mainEntity.name: Why does a freshly resurfaced pool crack within weeks or months, and is that always an installer problem?
mainEntity.text: Why does a freshly resurfaced pool crack within weeks or months, and is that always an installer problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fresh plaster cracks for several common reasons. Rapid drying from heat or wind, delayed refilling, poor curing conditions, movement in the pool shell, and aggressive startup chemistry can all stress the new surface. In Southern California, sun exposure and low humidity can make curing more difficult if the pool is not filled on time. Some minor shrinkage or crazing may be cosmetic, but cracks that widen, repeat, or appear along a pattern often indicate a deeper issue such as poor bond, substrate movement, or a shell defect. The key is to document when the crack appeared, how fast it is changing, and whether it is paired with hollow sounds or rough patches. Homeowners should also verify that the startup instructions were followed exactly, including brushing and water balance. If the problem appears soon after completion, a professional inspection should check both workmanship and structural causes.
acceptedAnswer.description: New plaster can crack from rapid drying, improper curing, early exposure to air, substrate movement, or water chemistry problems during startup. Not every crack means the installer failed, but large or growing cracks usually signal a preparation, curing, or structural issue. Small shrinkage lines may be cosmetic; wider cracks need inspection.
